factual_methodology.summary: ISM Services, ISM Manufacturing, S&P Global manufacturing, BLS employment, TSE election results and BCB Focus are first-party or primary sources. Intraday market levels are clearly time-bounded and sourced separately rather than presented as official closing data.

novelty.summary: The 5 October lead moves beyond the 4 October OPEC+ decision. The new analytical delta is the collision between still-expansionary U.S. services and global manufacturing, exceptionally high business price diffusion, weak U.S. payroll growth, elevated long yields, and Brazil's post-first-round repricing.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening states the regime directly, separates current data from inference, treats intraday prices as provisional and avoids turning the Brazil market reaction into a forecast of electoral or fiscal outcomes.

contextual_depth.summary: The brief connects labour, business surveys, inflation transmission, long rates, energy, global industrial demand and Brazil's election/expectations shock through explicit mechanisms and falsifiers.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 evidence table + 4 explicit charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Visual floor for a brief is exceeded. Diffusion-index charts use compatible units; the Brazil vote-share chart uses TSE percentages; qualitative map and flow reproduce mechanisms stated in prose.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The selected PMI measures use different survey populations and should be read directionally. Market prices in prose are intraday and are not used in quantitative charts.

contrary_evidence: Weak September payroll growth points toward softer future U.S. demand even while PMIs remain expansionary.
The U.S. services employment index returned slightly above 50, so the survey does not confirm a broad services employment contraction in September.
Oil eased from weekend risk levels on 5 October, which limits any claim of a new immediate energy shock despite still-high absolute prices.
Brazil's one-day market repricing does not establish a durable fiscal regime or the outcome of the 25 October runoff.
limitations: Intraday market prices can change materially before the 5 October close.
PMI diffusion indexes measure breadth and direction, not output growth rates directly; S&P Global's almost-4% global production figure is an empirical mapping from the survey output index.
The Focus survey released on 5 October reflects expectations collected before the 4 October Brazilian election and should not be interpreted as a post-election consensus.
Election-driven market moves reveal repricing of probabilities, not proof of future policy implementation.
notes: Approved for same-day publication after taxonomy normalization. Geography now uses the controlled Latin America & Caribbean subregion and structured ISO alpha-2 country objects; all material claims and source blobs are unchanged.

en.title: Global Macro — activity remains firm, service prices reaccelerate and markets test how much relief weaker labour really allows
en.deck: U.S. services remain in expansion and global manufacturing is at its strongest since 2022, while weak payrolls, high business price indexes, 5%+ long yields and Brazil's post-election repricing create a more unstable policy mix.
en.regime: Activity remains expansionary across U.S. services and global manufacturing while labour demand softens before business price pressure and long-term financing costs have normalized.
en.key_risk: Markets may be pricing monetary relief from weaker labour faster than inflationary cost pressure is actually fading, leaving both duration-sensitive assets and highly valued equities exposed to a renewed rates shock.

pt-BR.title: Macro Global — atividade permanece firme, preços de serviços reaceleram e mercados testam quanto alívio o trabalho mais fraco realmente permite
pt-BR.deck: Serviços dos EUA seguem em expansão e a manufatura global está no nível mais forte desde 2022, enquanto payroll fraco, índices elevados de preços, juros longos acima de 5% e o repricing pós-eleição no Brasil criam uma combinação de política mais instável.
pt-BR.regime: A atividade permanece em expansão nos serviços dos EUA e na manufatura global enquanto a demanda por trabalho enfraquece antes de a pressão de preços empresariais e o custo de financiamento de longo prazo normalizarem.
pt-BR.key_risk: Os mercados podem estar precificando alívio monetário a partir do trabalho mais fraco mais rapidamente do que a inflação de custos está desaparecendo, deixando ativos sensíveis à duração e ações de valuation elevado expostos a novo choque de juros.
